_why: ONE machine-readable statement of what the loop currently claims. Added by Exp857 after finding that RESULTS.md's headline still read '12.24 -> 2.70 (-78 %)' and .auto/prompt.md's 'Current best' still read '2.18 (MAX-SPEED v4.5)' two full eras after v4.6 (tail flush, Exp829) and v4.7 (boundary batch, Exp835) shipped - i.e. the measured TABLE cells were refreshed at Exp845/847 while the PROSE that a fresh session reads first was not, and the audit's 87 checks could not see it because check 4b only greps prompt.md for the shipped VAE *filename*. audit_harness.py check 9 now fails any 'current' prose number that disagrees with this file. Doc-drift trigger: when you ship, edit this file first, then let check 9 tell you which prose sites are stale.
_rule: Every value here is a MEASURED cell, not a target. Cells quoted from a single session are marked in provenance. Refresh on the doc-drift trigger (a shipped change that moves a ladder cell or the era).
regime: fresh-boot (device uptime 19 h at Exp944; the SAME byte-identical binary read 1.85 on the pre-reboot long-uptime device - Exp880 showed the device state, not the code, moved the metric)

shipped.label: MAX-SPEED v4.8, ARMED measurement state (burst + KEYCODE_WAKEUP stream, Exp979 recipe)
shipped.provenance: rtf10 = 1.2440/1.2533/1.2465 (three armed reps, Exp979/980) -> 1.25; ladder cells from ONE ascending armed session (Exp980): 1.2465 / 1.4648 / 1.5619 / 1.6478, canaries 39/106/446/876 exact, RSS 2191.7-2206.0 MB, majflt 0. WAIT-VALUE NOTE: the historical 1.1937 10 s cell (Exp939) was measured at mean delivered ~2377 MHz; the armed cells run at mean ~2045 MHz (same binary, lower P-state), which is the uniform +3..6 % seen on every cell. The unarmed counterpart of the same recipe reads 1.3385 (mean 1904 MHz) - the guard prints a WARNING when that happens, so a published cell must name its witness. gate mean/WER from Exp944 (gate944, 40/40, paired b=0/c=0 of 731 vs gate941 AND gate852, 0/40 differing); no src/ or tier file changed in Exp968-980, so no re-gate was owed
shipped.state_levels: THREE device states, each settable and recorded (Exp968-980). state 3 BOOST: protocol 1.22-1.25, mean delivered 2045-2377 MHz, screen ON + recent user activity. state 2 UNARMED: 1.67-1.70, mean ~1790 MHz, screen ON with no recent activity. state 1 SCREEN OFF: 1.85, mean ~1280 MHz. Long cells decay out of state 3 unless the activity STREAM continues (69 s: 2.05 unarmed -> 1.54 armed; 138 s: 2.14 -> 1.61, Exp978).

device_state._why: Exp968-980 turned 'the metric is 1.19 or 1.85 and nobody knows why' into a three-state model with a per-run witness. Before Exp972 the loop never recorded the display state at all, and before Exp975 it recorded only the 2.4 GHz share - which reads 0 % for a 2.15 GHz run and so mislabelled the fastest long cells of the day as 'capped' (Exp974).

states.boost: rtf10 1.22-1.25 | mean 2045-2377 MHz | screen ON + recent user activity; the state every historical ladder cell was taken in
states.unarmed: rtf10 1.67-1.70 | mean ~1790 MHz | screen ON, no recent activity
states.screen_off: rtf10 1.85 | mean ~1280 MHz | display off (and the historical 'long-uptime regime' 1.85 is this state, not silicon drift)

device_state.arm_recipe: measure.sh arms before every run: KEYCODE_WAKEUP + three volume pairs (UI-indifferent) to ARM, then a KEYCODE_WAKEUP stream every 3 s spanning the run to HOLD, sentinel-stopped. NO_ARM=1 disables it; ARM_STREAM=0 keeps burst-only. A volume-pair-only burst (the Exp972 recipe) lifted the state once and then stopped working after ~1500 events (Exp977/979).
device_state.witnesses: cpu7_deliv2400_pct (share of the 2.4 GHz step - NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: reads 0 % at 2.15 GHz), cpu7_deliv_mhz (MEAN delivered MHz - the number that names the P-state; 16th TSV column) and cpu7_deliv_ge2000_pct (share >= 2.0 GHz). GUARD: an armed run whose mean is below 2000 MHz prints a WARNING and must not be compared with boosted cells.
device_state.reliability: the arm is NOT 100 % effective: the protocol cell has read 1.2465 and 1.3385 (mean 1904) on consecutive runs, so a cell is a sample from a two-level state unless the witness is checked.
device_state.rule: quote the state (and its witness) with every speed number; never average a low-witness cell with boosted ones; the WER gate is state-independent (12 consecutive gates identical).
